title: Extended family, Polish mother, and his parents' deaths
summary: His father was of German extraction, his mother was born in Poland to a large family, a connection that warms Polish audiences; she died years ago and his father about seven or eight years earlier.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I see. Did you have -- well, did your parents have brothers and sisters?
My -- yes, they both had -- my father had a brother and a sister, a small family. And my mother came from a family of, I think, about nine or ten.
Oh, really?
Yeah.
Did any of them live nearby then?
Yeah, we used to get together with some of them, but not as realistically as -- with my father's side of the family because my mother's side of the family, not many of them spoke English at all.
Oh, I see.
They spoke Polish or sometimes, German.
And what extraction was your father?
He was of German extraction.
He was German.
But his family was third generation American.
I see.
And she was born -- my mother was born in Poland and came here as a baby. And this is something that the people in Poland are much aware of, and it makes her a very warm kind of situation.
I see. That's why there's interest and reception for you over there.
Yes.
Uh-huh. Is she still alive?
No, she passed away quite a number of years ago. And my Dad I lost about seven, eight years ago.
And you used to visit him, I recall.
Yeah.
In a rest home or --

At the end, yeah. But prior to that, he managed to live in apartment hotels, and earlier he got his own place. And he was very self sufficient, and he had a good life until the final breakdown when he broke a leg and a hip-bone and a few things, and it was the point of no return. But that's when he had to go in the rest home.
